description: Recommend buying 21 diesel and 5 gas Access Transit buses.
Funded by $23.5 million borrowing and $23,900 from reserves.
Addresses federal funding denial and bus delivery delays.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Saskatoon's electric buses experienced power train issues; winter performance needs assessment.
Taxpayers will fund $23.5 million through city borrowing for bus purchases.
Federal zero-emission transit funding was denied, impacting the city's fleet transition.
Administration will present an updated 10-year fleet renewal strategy in Q2 2025.

segments.title: Saskatoon Transit 2025 Fleet Renewal Request
segments.takeaway: Administration presented the 2025 fleet renewal request, detailing funding changes due to ZETETF denial, current bus purchases, and recommending Option 1 for diesel and access transit buses.

segments.title: Committee questions on fleet renewal
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on fleet size, delivery times, ridership, alternative fuel options, the zero-emission fund denial, and the budget implications of the proposed plan.

segments.title: Vote on 2025 fleet renewal
segments.takeaway: The committee unanimously approved the administration's recommendation to proceed with the procurement of 21 diesel and 3 access transit buses for the 2025 fleet renewal.

description: Saskatoon will permit shared e-scooters on public roads.
City will select up to two e-scooter vendors.
Traffic Bylaw 7200 will be amended for e-scooters.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
Councillor Donauer questioned the five-year term
Nearly 20,000 unique riders used shared e-scooters last year.
City Solicitor stated holding vendors accountable for rider actions would be extremely difficult.
Unknown how many e-scooter ER visits were due to not wearing a helmet.
City surveys showed 53-64% public support for continuing the e-scooter program.
226 riders used a reduced price option for e-scooter access.
E-scooter use estimated to have averted 40 tons of CO2 emissions.
Administration will bring a report on private e-scooters by late spring/early summer 2025.

speakers.name: Isaac Ransom
speakers.summary: Isaac Ransom, Neuron Mobility, spoke in support of the Program with a PowerPoint and responded to questions of Committee.
said: Program generated $5.6M local economic impact last year.
80% of trips wouldn't happen without scooters; half replace car journeys.
Neuron provides helmets on every scooter and uses geofencing.

segments.title: Shared Electric Kick Scooter Program Pilot Overview
segments.takeaway: Administration presented a report detailing the two-year shared electric kick scooter pilot program, including its framework, operational statistics, survey results, and recommendations for continuati

segments.title: Neuron Mobility Presentation and Committee Questions
segments.takeaway: Isaac Ransom from Neuron Mobility presented on their operations, economic impact, and safety initiatives, followed by committee questions regarding parking, helmet use, and liability.

segments.title: Committee Questions for Administration
segments.takeaway: Committee members questioned administration on vendor selection, fees, helmet enforcement, geofencing effectiveness, and the future consideration of private e-scooters.

segments.title: Committee Discussion and Program Continuation Vote
segments.takeaway: The committee discussed concerns about helmet use, vendor accountability, and contract terms, ultimately voting unanimously to continue the shared electric kick scooter program.
